font.whatIsBuljirya: Buljirya is a real typeface, and the spelling is correct. It is not Korean. It is "Buljirya Modern Serif Font" by Hishand Studio (Dody Permana, Indonesia), first published in July 2021. It is a display serif in the fashion/Didone style: very high stroke contrast, thick stems with hairline serifs and joins, generous caps, and playful alternates (a long-tailed j, a curled y, a swash a), plus ligatures and a separate line-icon font (arches, moons, sparkles). The foundry describes it as "inspired by dream and pastel colour combined with elegance... for logo, packaging, fashion brand, magazine headers". The full family has Regular, Italic and Icon. Sources: https://hishandstudio.com/product/buljirya-modern-serif-font/ , https://www.dafont.com/buljirya.font , https://fontesk.com/buljirya-font/ , https://befonts.com/buljirya-font.html , https://www.fontriver.com/font/buljirya/ . I viewed the specimen images (fontesk buljirya.jpg, buljirya-2.jpg and the Hishand product images). The Korean search "불지르야" only returned news about arson ("불 지르겠다"), and the alternate spellings Buljiriya, Bulgirya and Buljira returned no web results. "Buljirya" is the Hishand font.
font.buljiryaSupportsVietnamese: No, not in any version I could verify. The free demo (Buljirya.otf, about 222 glyphs) covers only Basic Latin and Latin-1 (À–ÿ). It also has a few combining marks (U+0300/0301/0302/0303/0304/0307/0308/030A/030C/0327), going by the befonts charmap at https://befonts.com/buljirya-font.html (dafont lists "View all glyphs (223)"). It lacks ă/Ă, ơ/Ơ, ư/Ư and đ/Đ, the precomposed U+1EA0–1EF9 range, and the combining hook-above (U+0309), dot-below (U+0323) and horn (U+031B). So it cannot set Vietnamese, even with combining marks. The paid version only says "multilingual support" and names no languages, and none of its product images show Vietnamese text. Treat it as unsupported unless the foundry confirms otherwise (contact: dodypermana73@gmail.com).
font.buljiryaUsableOnWeb: Not as a free font. The dafont/fontesk/befonts download is a demo "FREE FOR PERSONAL USE ONLY. NO COMMERCIAL USE ALLOWED", so it can't go on a public portfolio that funnels readers to products on ceovanta.com. Hishand sells a Web Font License for $36; the $18 Standard License explicitly "does not cover: Website Usage" (https://hishandstudio.com/product/buljirya-modern-serif-font/). It is not on Google Fonts or Fontsource. Even with the web licence, the missing Vietnamese glyphs would make every heading on the Vietnamese-default site fall back to another font for ă, ơ, ư, đ and the stacked tone marks. Recommendation: don't use Buljirya. Use a free OFL font with the same look and full Vietnamese coverage (below).

candidates.source: Google Fonts: https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Noto+Serif+Display ; Fontsource @fontsource-variable/noto-serif-display@5.3.0 (ships vietnamese-wght/wdth normal+italic woff2)

candidates.resemblance: Closest overall match. A high-contrast Didone-style display serif with hairline serifs and thick stems. At 300–400 weight it matches Buljirya's 'Buljirya'/'WELTON BERSKA' specimens. Thin/ExtraLight gives the airy fashion-magazine feel, and the wdth axis (62.5–100) gives condensed poster caps. It has no quirky swash alternates; that personality would have to come from the layout.
candidates.license: SIL Open Font License 1.1 (free for web/commercial)

candidates.evidence: curl of css2?family=Playfair:ital,opsz,wdth,wght@0,5..1200,87.5..112.5,300..900;1,5..1200,87.5..112.5,300..900: HTTP 200, two /* vietnamese */ blocks. Rendered at opsz 5/144/1200 to confirm the opsz axis works. The Vietnamese stacks (ẫ ự đ, Kiến thức Đẳng cấp italic) are clean.
candidates.resemblance: A refined transitional/Didone serif with opsz, wdth and wght (down to 300) axes. The italic is the most expressive and calligraphic of the set and comes closest to Buljirya's flowing alternates. Contrast is softer than Buljirya even at opsz 1200.

candidates.evidence: curl of css2?family=Playfair+Display:ital,wght@0,400..900;1,400..900: HTTP 200, two /* vietnamese */ blocks. Rendered: strong, well-placed stacked marks (ễ ẫ ổ with the tilde above the circumflex).
candidates.resemblance: The classic high-contrast Didone with ball terminals. Its contrast is closest to Buljirya's thick-stem/hairline rhythm, but it is heavier (minimum weight 400) and very widely used, so it reads as more generic than the others.

candidates.evidence: curl of css2?family=Imbue:opsz,wght@10..100,100..900: HTTP 200, one /* vietnamese */ block (no italic exists). Rendered at opsz 100 / 200: Việt Nguyễn ệ ề ể ẫ ộ ỗ Ượ all clean.
candidates.resemblance: A condensed fashion-poster Didone with hairline thins: strong editorial/fashion character. Its proportions are much narrower than Buljirya's, so it suits short hero words and stacked titles rather than long headings.

candidates.evidence: curl of css2?family=Fraunces:ital,opsz,wght,SOFT,WONK@0,9..144,100..900,0..100,0..1;1,...: HTTP 200, two /* vietnamese */ blocks. Rendered at opsz 144, 300, SOFT 50, WONK 1: all Vietnamese stacks are clean.
candidates.resemblance: The most 'artistic' option. The WONK axis gives leaning, quirky letterforms (n, h, m) and SOFT rounds the terminals. That echoes Buljirya's playful alternates more than its Didone structure. Lower contrast than Buljirya.

candidates.evidence: curl of css2?family=Cormorant:ital,wght@0,300..700;1,300..700 and the same for Cormorant Garamond: HTTP 200, /* vietnamese */ blocks present. But in the headless-Chrome render at 300 weight, ệ and ộ (circumflex + dot below) get a tall narrow pointed caret that doesn't match ề/ể/ẫ. That is visible in 'Việt' and 'liệu'.
candidates.resemblance: The airiest, most hairline option, with the elegant Garamond-derived calligraphic feel. Visually very close to Buljirya's dreamy mood. It is ranked last because the inconsistent ệ/ộ marks would show on common Vietnamese words (Việt, liệu, hộ).

candidates.evidence: curl of css2?family=Be+Vietnam+Pro:ital,wght@0,300;0,400;0,500;0,600;0,700;1,400: HTTP 200, /* vietnamese */ block for every weight, unicode-range U+0102-0103, U+0110-0111, U+01A0-01A1, U+01AF-01B0, U+0300-0301, U+0303-0304, U+0308-0309, U+0323, U+1EA0-1EF9. Rendered a body paragraph and tracked caps on dark: comfortable and clean.
candidates.resemblance: A neo-grotesque sans built specifically for Vietnamese, with vertical metrics that fit stacked tone marks. Clean and geometric like the reference image's nav and buttons, and clearly distinct from a hairline Didone display. It works for UI, nav, glass buttons, the wide-tracked hero subtitle and long notes.

candidates.resemblance: Not Buljirya-like. It is a sturdy text serif for long notes. It can stay if the owner prefers serif reading, but alongside a serif display it is a less distinct pairing than a sans body.

font.recommendedPairing:
Two families, clearly distinct (frontend-design: "use one family or two, and if two, make them clearly distinct"):
- DISPLAY: Noto Serif Display. Hero/H1 at weight 300–400, wdth 100. Condensed caps (wdth 62.5–75) only for one poster-style moment. Italic for the occasional pull quote.
- UI + BODY: Be Vietnam Pro. Nav, buttons, filters, search, tables, and long notes at 17–18px / line-height 1.7 / max about 68ch, weight 400 body, 500–600 UI.
Exact URL (verified HTTP 200, 8 /* vietnamese */ blocks):
https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Noto+Serif+Display:ital,wdth,wght@0,62.5..100,100..900;1,62.5..100,100..900&family=Be+Vietnam+Pro:ital,wght@0,300;0,400;0,500;0,600;0,700;1,400&display=swap

CSS tokens: --display: 'Noto Serif Display', 'Playfair Display', Georgia, serif; --sans: 'Be Vietnam Pro', system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif.

Notes:
- On the dark violet background, keep display weight at 300 or above below about 48px; Thin/ExtraLight hairlines disappear at small sizes.
- Use the reference's wide-tracked subtitle (Be Vietnam Pro 500, letter-spacing about .3em, uppercase) once in the hero, not as an eyebrow on every section; the skill flags tracked all-caps eyebrows as a templated tell.
- If the owner wants serif reading for long notes, keep Source Serif 4 for .prose only by appending &family=Source+Serif+4:ital,opsz,wght@0,8..60,400..700;1,8..60,400. That makes three families, which is acceptable but less distinct.
- To reduce the dependency on fonts.googleapis.com, self-host instead with @fontsource-variable/noto-serif-display@5.3.0 and @fontsource/be-vietnam-pro@5.3.0; both ship Vietnamese woff2 files.
- Alternative display if more personality is wanted: Playfair (2.0) italic, or Fraunces with WONK 1 for a quirkier look.

Excluded lookalikes: none of these has a vietnamese subset in css2 (checked with curl): Bodoni Moda, Gloock, Italiana, DM Serif Display, Instrument Serif, Gilda Display, Young Serif, Abril Fatface, Marcellus, Cinzel, Bellefair, Libre Caslon Display, Syne, Sora, Outfit, DM Sans.

images.imageQualityNotes:
Counts come from a python script over /Users/pc/Desktop/Sky/portfolio-site/src/content/blog. It found 300 .md files, of which 57 have isIndex: true and were excluded, leaving 243 posts. Of those, 74 reference /vault-assets/ at least once, with 320 references in total (biology alone has 283).

public/vault-assets holds 306 files, about 62 MB: 143 JPG (52 MB), 98 PNG (9.3 MB) and 65 SVG (0.6 MB). sync-vault.mjs only shrinks rasters over 300 KB to 1600 px, so many JPGs are still 500–830 KB. There are no WebP files and no thumbnails.

What the first image of each of the 74 posts is:
- 26 hand-made SVG diagrams, all from the Kiến thức chung notes.
- 26 phone photos: 20 portrait 3:4 and 6 landscape. They show lab plates, specimens, handwritten lab reports, photos of projected slides, and field shots of bats, birds and plants. The 4 French posts are photos of handwritten essays.
- 22 PNG screenshots: 11 very wide (wider than 2:1, e.g. 1943x353 tables) and 10 landscape. Some are tiny (473x170), and some are blurry textbook scans from the Tsing Hua posts.

Images I opened:
- public/vault-assets/bat-1-hipposideros-sp1-143972ff.jpg (2048x1365): a bat on a cave ceiling lit by a flashlight, with a dark vignette. This is the best atmospheric photo and fits a dark theme as a cover.
- public/vault-assets/img-4180-576a2c66.jpg (1200x1600): a 24-well plate with handwritten Vietnamese labels on a wooden table. Clean; works as a square-cropped thumbnail.
- public/vault-assets/img-4985-0facdc0f.jpg (1600x1200): red Ardisia berries, colourful, but classmates' arms and a Red Bull can are in frame. Needs cropping.
- public/vault-assets/bird-1-male-a-d7cb3f97.jpg (1600x1066): the sunbird is barely visible in the foliage. Only useful as a green texture or duotone background.
- public/vault-assets/img-5834-0379b816.jpg (2048x1536): a photo of a projected karyotype-banding slide with a classmate's head in the foreground. Unsuitable as a cover, for privacy and quality.
- public/vault-assets/dvcxs-img-4277-ebdc5e54.jpg (1200x1600): a handwritten lab report page. Text, not imagery, so a poor cover.
- public/vault-assets/image-016-43528d0a.png (1943x353): a screenshot of a "Data Analysis Process" table. Unusable as a thumbnail.
- public/vault-assets/anh-chup-man-hinh-2026-09-14-luc-23-35-28-dfb5c5da.png: a blurry scanned textbook flowchart. Low quality.
- public/vault-assets/hinh-cau-truc-ti-the-5b4f7447.svg (960x440): a mitochondria diagram, crisp and labelled in Vietnamese. It has a hard-coded light background (#fbfaf7), Helvetica text and a warm orange/purple palette, so in a dark redesign it will sit as a bright card.

Verdict:
- Only about 20–30 photos are good enough for cards or covers, mostly from the field studies, zoology and botany.
- Screenshots, tables, handwritten pages and slide photos should never be auto-used as thumbnails.
- The 65 SVG diagrams are good inline figures but need a frame or recolour so they don't clash with a dark page.
- Some photos show classmates (img-5834, img-4985), so a manual privacy pass is needed before anything is shown on cards.
- Base.astro has no og:image or twitter:image tags at all.

proposals.idea: Seeded procedural cover art for every post and topic: iridescent fluid blobs plus a thin white wireframe polyhedron with vertex dots, echoing the reference image. Each topic gets its own galaxy arm colour (biology = lime/cyan, french = magenta, ai-development = violet, business = amber, university-courses = coral, english = cyan), so covers match the galaxy.
proposals.where: Blog list and topic list rows (a 64–96 px glyph, or a wide card on desktop), topic page headers, post header banners, and the fallback for any post without a real photo.
proposals.how: A new Astro component, e.g. <Cover seed={slug} topic={topic} variant='thumb'|'banner' />, rendered as inline SVG at build time with no runtime JS. A hash of the slug seeds a small PRNG that picks 3–5 blob centres, radii and gradient stops from the topic palette. Blobs are radialGradient circles merged by feGaussianBlur plus feColorMatrix (gooey effect), with an optional feTurbulence grain. The wireframe is a projected icosahedron or octahedron with a random rotation, drawn as 1 px white lines at about 0.5 opacity plus white dots. A slow CSS drift or hue-rotate runs only under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference. Covers are decorative, so aria-hidden and empty alt.
proposals.cost: About 4–6 hours. Roughly 2–4 KB of SVG per inline cover, or emit /covers/<slug>.svg files from sync-vault.mjs so they can be cached. No new dependencies. Covers 100% of the 243 posts and is visually consistent by construction.

proposals.idea: Real-photo thumbnails from the first suitable image in a note, with a neon duotone treatment so mixed phone photos look like one set.
proposals.where: Cards for the roughly 25–30 lab and field posts (biology-project-and-lab-report: biological-field-study, vertebrate/invertebrate zoology, botany, ecology), plus covers on those posts' pages.
proposals.how: In scripts/sync-vault.mjs, pick the first /vault-assets/ JPG whose aspect ratio is 0.6–1.8. Skip anh-chup-man-hinh-*, image-*, pasted-image-* and SVGs. Write it as a `cover:` frontmatter field, and let a vault-side `cover:` or `cover: none` override it. Add `cover: z.string().optional()` to the base schema in src/content.config.ts. Generate 480 px and 960 px WebP into public/vault-thumbs/ with sharp, which is already in node_modules as an Astro dependency. Render with width and height attributes, loading=lazy and decoding=async, and a CSS duotone: a grayscale image under an overlay in the topic colour with mix-blend-mode: color or screen, or an SVG feColorMatrix filter. Show true colour on hover or focus. Keep a manual exclude list for photos with classmates (e.g. img-5834-0379b816.jpg, img-4985-0facdc0f.jpg uncropped).
proposals.cost: About 3–4 hours of code plus about 1 hour of curation and privacy review. Each thumbnail is about 25–60 KB. Covers only about 25–30 posts, so it must sit on top of the procedural covers, not replace them.

proposals.idea: Project cover art: the Virtual Lab isometric machine, and generative data art for the two case studies until real charts exist.
proposals.where: Project cards on the home page and /projects, plus the ProjectCase.astro header, inside the existing brutalist frame (thick border, hard shadow) so projects keep their distinct look.
proposals.how: Virtual Lab: export the dark thermocycler or geldoc figure from /Users/pc/Desktop/Sky/Virtual_Lab/figures to a static image. Either take a headless Chrome screenshot (claude-in-chrome or a one-off Playwright run) and save it as WebP, or extract the inline <svg> and its CSS variables into a static SVG. Put it in public/project-covers/ and add a `cover` field to the projects schema. Cyclistic and Track B: draw seeded SVG art in the neon palette, e.g. route-like Bezier strands, or a radial 24-hour histogram drawn as wireframe spokes for Cyclistic. Swap in the real Tableau or matplotlib figures once the figures/ folders are filled (the deadlines are this month).
proposals.cost: About 2 hours for Virtual Lab (one WebP of about 80–150 KB, or a 270–530 KB SVG that would need trimming) and about 2–3 hours for the two generative covers. Replacing them with real charts later means editing one frontmatter field each.

proposals.idea: Hero imagery inspired by the reference: fluid iridescent blobs and white wireframe polyhedra built into the existing Three.js galaxy, so the hero and the site share one visual language instead of a dark hero over a light page.
proposals.where: The home page hero (Galaxy.astro). Optionally a static, blurred echo of the same blobs as the page background glow on other pages.
proposals.how: In the existing Three.js scene, add 1–2 IcosahedronGeometry meshes drawn with EdgesGeometry and LineBasicMaterial (white, about 0.4 opacity), plus Points at the vertices, rotating slowly around the galaxy core. Behind the canvas, add CSS blobs: absolutely positioned divs with radial-gradient fills in the arm colours, filter: blur(40–60 px), and keyframes that animate border-radius and transform, or one SVG with feTurbulence plus feDisplacementMap. Under prefers-reduced-motion, freeze rotation and keyframes and show a single static frame. Keep the galaxy as the one focal element: the blobs are a soft background and the wireframes are thin.
proposals.cost: About 3–4 hours. No new library, since three@0.187 is already loaded. Background blobs cost little GPU when limited to 3–4 elements; animate only transform and opacity on mobile at 390 px.

proposals.idea: Dark-theme treatment for the 65 hand-made SVG diagrams inside posts, so they don't show as white rectangles on a deep indigo page.
proposals.where: Kiến thức chung biology notes: 26 posts, 2–5 diagrams each.
proposals.how: Phase 1, zero risk: a CSS 'specimen plate' frame for img[src$='.svg'] in post bodies: a light rounded plate (they already use #fbfaf7) inside a frosted-glass border with a soft violet glow and a caption from the alt text. It reads like a slide on a dark page. Phase 2, optional: in sync-vault.mjs, rewrite the fills with a colour map (#fbfaf7 → transparent or #161337, #333 and #555 text → #ecebff, the orange #e08a2e and purple #7d55b8 strokes → neon amber and violet) and inline the result so it can follow the theme.
proposals.cost: Phase 1 is about 30–45 minutes of CSS. Phase 2 is about 3 hours plus a visual check of all 65 diagrams, with a risk of contrast regressions in labels; do it only if phase 1 still clashes.

proposals.idea: A curated 'Lab & field' gallery, which is the most authentic imagery the owner has: bats in caves, birds, Ardisia berries, Trametes fungi, specimen plates, the museum visit.
proposals.where: A home page strip under the galaxy (4–6 photos), or a /gallery page, with each photo linking back to its note (e.g. biological-field-study/anh-thuc-dia.md, which has 32 images, and vertebrate-zoology/06-tham-quan-bao-tang-dong-vat.md, which has 12).
proposals.how: A hand-picked list of 20–30 file names in site.config.json, rendered as a CSS columns masonry using the WebP thumbnails from the photo-thumbnail proposal. Apply the duotone at rest and true colour on hover or focus (focus-visible ring). Captions use the note title. Under reduced motion there are no hover transitions.
proposals.cost: About 2–3 hours, including curation. Depends on the WebP thumbnail pipeline from the photo-thumbnail proposal.

proposals.idea: Per-post social and OG images, which are missing today.
proposals.how: Reuse the procedural cover SVG at 1200x630 and rasterize it with sharp during sync or build into public/og/<slug>.png. Option A: no title text (cover art plus a small wordmark path), which avoids font problems. Option B: include the title, which requires embedding a Vietnamese-capable font as outlined paths or with satori plus resvg, a new dependency. Satori needs the font's TTF with full Vietnamese coverage, including ặ ẫ ở ữ ự đ.

proposals.idea: An image-weight fix to do first, before adding more images.
proposals.where: public/vault-assets (62 MB) and the post bodies.
proposals.how: In sync-vault.mjs, also write .webp versions (sharp, quality about 78, max 1600 px) and cap the long edge at 1600 for every image, not only files over 300 KB. Add a small rehype plugin that adds loading=lazy, decoding=async, width and height to every , and wraps it in with a WebP source.

images.recommendation: Build the seeded procedural cover system first. It is the only option that gives every post an image (169 of 243 posts have none, and all 13 business and 2 english posts have none). It matches the reference look (fluid blobs plus white wireframes in the galaxy's neon colours) and costs no runtime JS. Then add three things on top. First, real-photo thumbnails only for the roughly 25–30 good lab and field photos, with a neon duotone and a manual privacy pass, because some photos show classmates. Second, the Virtual Lab isometric figure as that project's cover. Third, the same wireframe and blob motifs in the galaxy hero, so the hero and the rest of the site look like one system. Never auto-use screenshots, tables, handwritten pages or slide photos as thumbnails. Frame the 65 light SVG diagrams as 'specimen plates' so they don't clash with a dark page. Before any of this, add the WebP plus lazy-loading step, because the asset folder is already 62 MB. Leave the Cyclistic and Track B covers procedural until their real charts exist, then swap them in.

audit.referenceAnalysis:
"FLUID TECHNOLOGY" reference (1290x740 landing page). It is dark throughout, with one violet glow, iridescent liquid on the right, white wireframes and frosted-glass bars.

BACKGROUND. Deep indigo-violet, never black.
- Edges and right side: about #0e0330 to #120438.
- Upper band above the header: #1c0846.
- Radial glow sits behind the headline, centred near x=25% y=45%: core about #5a14b0, midway #2e0a6e, fading into #10042f by about 55% width. The glow sits behind the TEXT, not behind the blobs, so the copy reads against the brightest part of the background. White text on the glow core is about 11.6:1, so contrast is not a problem.

BLOBS. About 7 organic liquid blobs plus 3 small spheres, stacked in a vertical column on the right 45%. They bleed off the top and bottom edges and pass under both glass bars.
- Iridescent multi-stop gradients that shift along each form: hot pink #f45fd0, magenta-lilac #d95bf0 / #b18cff, sky cyan #4ccfff, aqua #5be3f0, amber #ffc94a, gold #f7a531, with peach #ff9e9e transitions.
- A soft white specular rim (about 60–70% white) on the lit edge gives volume. There are no hard outlines.
- Depth comes from 2–3 out-of-focus blobs (gaussian blur about 20–30px, amber/teal, lower saturation) behind the sharp ones, like a depth-of-field effect.
- Spheres are 60–90px pink→amber and lilac→white orbs.
- These hues map almost 1:1 onto the galaxy arm neons: magenta #ff3db4, violet #a78bfa, cyan #2ef2ff, amber #ffb627, coral #ff6b5e.

WIREFRAMES. 5–6 low-poly polyhedra (tetrahedra, octahedra, irregular hulls) scattered across and over the blobs.
- Hairline white lines, about 1px at about 80–90% opacity.
- Solid white vertex dots, about 4–5px.
- Some faces filled with very faint translucent white (about 10–20%), like glass panes.
- They cross in front of some blobs and behind others, so they interleave in depth. This is the same visual language as the site's constellation lines and star nodes.

GLASS. Header and footer are full-width translucent bars.
- Header: about 60px tall, inset about 25px from the top edge. Footer: about 75px, flush to the bottom.
- Fill is a vertical white gradient, about rgba(255,255,255,0.28) at the top to 0.10 at the bottom. Over the purple this reads about #6a5a8c→#3d2a66.
- No visible border; a lighter top edge acts as the highlight. Blobs show through, washed lighter (frosted).
- Buttons are small rectangles, about 120–165 x 40px, radius 0–2px, with the same top-lit glass gradient and 14px light text. The play button has a solid white circle icon.
- Social icons are 36px solid white rounded squares (radius about 8px) with purple glyphs.

TYPOGRAPHY. A geometric sans (Raleway-like), all white.
- Title "FLUID": about 150px, bold, caps, tight to normal tracking.
- Subtitle "TECHNOLOGY": about 40px (about 0.27x the title), medium weight, wide tracking about 0.18–0.2em, and the same width as the title. The title and subtitle lock up as one block.
- Body: about 14–15px light, about 1.9 line-height, white at about 85%, short measure (about 45ch).
- Nav: about 18px regular, white, gaps of about 50px.
- The user wants a more artistic face like "Buljirya". That is a 2021 Hishand Studio dreamy high-contrast display serif with soft curves and ligatures. It is licensed for personal use only and has only about 222 glyphs, so it has no Vietnamese ặ ẫ ở ữ ự. It cannot be used here.
- Close Google Fonts alternatives with a verified `vietnamese` subset (checked through the css2 API):
  - Fraunces (opsz 9–144, wght, SOFT 0–100, WONK 0–1). Best match: SOFT=100 with high opsz gives the soft, dreamy, curvy high-contrast look.
  - Playfair 2.0 (opsz to 1200, wdth).
  - Yeseva One, Prata, Cormorant.
- No Vietnamese subset (avoid): Bodoni Moda, DM Serif Display, Instrument Serif, Gloock, Young Serif, Abril Fatface, Italiana, Syne.
- Current fonts Bricolage Grotesque and Source Serif 4 both include Vietnamese.

LAYOUT AND SPACING. Asymmetric.
- Left text column starts about 6% from the left edge, is about 35% wide and vertically centred. The right 45% is the fluid composition, with an empty gutter of about 15% between them.
- Generous negative space, one focal cluster, no cards, no section dividers.

MOOD. Soft, liquid, luminous, layered in depth: glass over liquid over glow.

The galaxy is the only dark element on a white page, which is the core 'lệch pha' (out of phase). Even the existing dark set (--paper #17152b) is a flat grey-violet, not the reference's #0e0330 to #5a14b0 glow.

Fonts (Base.astro line 46 and the --sans/--serif tokens): add Fraunces as the display face (headings, wordmark, hero, CTA title) with SOFT 100, WONK 1 and opsz 144 at large sizes. Restrict the axis ranges in the css2 URL (for example wght 500..800, opsz 72..144) to keep payload down. Keep Source Serif 4 for long-form .prose (or move prose to Fraunces at text opsz with SOFT 0 and WONK 0, which drops to two families). Keep Bricolage Grotesque for UI, nav, labels and the wide-tracked hero subtitle. Raise display line-height to 1.1 or more and stop negative tracking below -0.02em for Vietnamese.

Base.astro .masthead / .masthead-inner / .nav / .toggles: a sticky frosted-glass bar with a top-lit gradient, -webkit-backdrop-filter and backdrop-filter blur(12px) saturate(140%), and an @supports fallback of rgba(20,10,50,.85). Wordmark in the display font; active nav item with a neon underline; .toggle as small glass chips. Decide the theme-toggle semantics (dark default, with optional light 'paper' reading mode), update the inline bootstrap script and the mermaid detection, and add <meta name=theme-color content=#0f0828>.

Base.astro .colophon: a glass footer bar. Turn author links into icon buttons (white rounded squares with indigo glyph, reference style) carrying text labels or aria-labels. Keep the RSS and CEOVANTA links.

index.astro hero (.hero, .intro, .actions): a full-bleed section outside .wrap, with an inner .wrap for the text. Text column on the left over the radial glow; galaxy canvas positioned right and bleeding to the viewport edge, under the glass header. Display h1 in Fraunces with a Bricolage subtitle lockup. Glass rectangular buttons, one of them filled with --iris. At 390px: headline first, then the galaxy edge-to-edge with no radius.

Galaxy.astro and the .galaxy/.g-* CSS: drop the boxed radius and aspect-ratio when it is used as the hero environment. Match scene.background to --void/--glow, or make the canvas transparent by outputting premultiplied alpha = glow intensity in starMat (today alpha is always 1.0, which is what causes the dark halos), and feather the edges with a CSS mask-image radial. Restyle the course constellations as reference wireframes (thin white lines, white vertex dots, faint glass faces). Add 3–5 iridescent blobs or nebula volumes in the same scene and WebGL context. Move .g-legend and figcaption into a glass strip inside the dark area. .g-tip and .g-controls are already glass and only need token alignment.

global.css .button / .button.solid / .actions: rectangular (radius about 2–4px) glass buttons with a top-lit white gradient and a 1px glass edge; .solid uses --iris with dark text (#14063a on magenta is 5.9:1, on cyan 13.7:1). Keep a 44px minimum touch height.

global.css .brutal block plus ProjectCase.astro, PhaseTrack.astro, projects/index.astro, projects/[...slug].astro (.article-head.brutal, .children.brutal, .actions.brutal): keep it brutalist but neon. Borders at 3px in --ink or a neon; hard offset shadows in --n-magenta / --n-cyan (for example 6px 6px 0 magenta, or a cyan+magenta split) instead of the white --ink; opaque --deep fill (not glass, for legibility). .status as a neon pill with dark text; .track bars filled with the --iris gradient; tags in the topic's arm colour.

Also reuse it as og:image in Base.astro and switch twitter:card to summary_large_image.

Cta.astro / .cta: the iridescent focal panel. An --iris gradient border or a glass panel over a soft blob, display-font title, solid white button with indigo text. Fix the hover state that puts #fff on eosin (2.44:1).

PostRows.astro / .rows, blog/index.astro .filters / .search / .result-count / .empty, topics/index.astro .topic-group: stay minimal. Colour change only: solid --deep input with a visible 1px edge, a coloured dot per topic using the arm colour, pressed filter chip in a neon outline with readable text. No glass, blur or motion here.

.article / .prose / .callout / .pager / .share / .crumbs / .byline (blog/[slug].astro, topics/[slug].astro, projects/[...slug].astro): a quiet reading surface. Solid --void, or a very subtle static glow far from the text column; off-white body text; serif at 19px/1.72 kept; neon only for links, list markers and the blockquote rule; .prose img framed as a light 'slide' (padding, radius, glass edge) so white screenshots and the 65 light SVG diagrams sit intentionally; tables and code with dark tokens; .share as glass pills. Move the inline style max-width:46rem (topics/[slug].astro) and margin-top/max-width (projects/[...slug].astro lines 37-39) into classes.

global.css .astro-code rules: apply the --shiki-dark colours and --code-bg by default under the dark-first tokens, so they no longer depend on [data-theme=dark] or prefers-color-scheme. Base.astro mermaid: use theme 'base' with themeVariables taken from the tokens, or 'dark' by default.
404.astro .page-head: dark minimal message with a clear back-home button. At most a small static wireframe glyph; no motion.
public/favicon.svg: redraw in indigo with neon dots (it can echo the galaxy).

scripts/sync-vault.mjs (or a rehype plugin in astro.config.mjs): emit loading=lazy, decoding=async and intrinsic width/height for vault images. Generate WebP/AVIF thumbnails (sharp) for any new imagery strip, for example the bird and bat field photos as a 'from the lab' band. Avoid the frog-dissection (dvcxs) photos as decorative imagery.
motionOpportunities: One orchestrated hero intro, the single non-user-triggered 'moment': the galaxy ignites from the core outward (a uTime uniform scales star size and alpha by radius over about 1.6s), while the display headline fades in with a gentle blur-to-sharp and the subtitle tracking settles from 0.3em to 0.18em. No per-section fade-ups after that.

Iridescent liquid blobs (the reference's main motif), in the arm palette, slowly drifting and morphing (20–40s loops) on the hero's right and passing under the glass header so the frost reveals them. Preferably done inside the existing Three.js scene (low-poly spheres displaced by noise in the vertex shader with a fresnel/iridescent gradient fragment), so it is one WebGL context. CSS fallback: pre-rendered gradient SVG/WebP blobs animated by transform only.

Reference wireframes: restyle the course constellations as thin white lines with white vertex dots and faint glass faces, and float 3–5 slowly rotating EdgesGeometry polyhedra (icosahedron, octahedron) around the galaxy, interleaved in depth with the blobs. This ties the decoration to real content, since the constellations are courses.
Pointer parallax (desktop, fine pointer only): blobs and polyhedra shift a few pixels against the cursor and the camera eases slightly. Disable for coarse pointers and under reduced motion.

Interaction feedback on the galaxy: hovering a .g-legend topic or a nav topic brightens that arm and draws its constellation in white; leaving fades it back. This motion answers an action and is the most informative one.

Scroll-linked exit, progressive enhancement: as the hero scrolls out, the camera dollies back a little and the glow dims, using CSS animation-timeline: view() or scroll() inside @supports, or a cheap rAF read of scrollY that feeds a uniform.
Glass buttons and CTA: a sheen sweep (translateX of a gradient pseudo-element) on hover and focus; the iris border of the CTA rotates slowly only while hovered.

Brutalist project cards (portfolio pages only): on hover or focus the hard neon shadow grows from 4px to 8px with a slight translate (this already exists in .brutal .button and can extend to .brutal .case). :active presses in.

PhaseTrack: progress bars fill to their value with the iris gradient the first time they enter the viewport (IntersectionObserver plus a transform: scaleX transition). This shows real data and is not decoration.

Cross-page View Transitions (@view-transition { navigation: auto; } or Astro ClientRouter): a quick crossfade, with the wordmark and header persisting between blog list and post. It must be turned off under reduced motion.

Glass header state: transparent over the hero, gaining frost and a hairline once the page scrolls past the hero. A single class toggled by IntersectionObserver on the hero, so the blur doesn't run over the animating canvas all the time.
risks: Specificity and gutter trap: .hero, .page-head and .article sit on the same element as .wrap (index.astro section.wrap.hero, 404.astro div.wrap.page-head, blog/topics/projects div.wrap.article) and are declared after .wrap and its 720px media rule with equal specificity. Today they set only padding-top/padding-bottom longhands, which is safe. Any redesign that writes a padding shorthand there (for example .hero { padding: 96px 0 }) silently zeroes the 16/32px horizontal gutter and text touches the edge at 390px. The same applies to div.wrap.brutal (projects/index.astro) if .brutal ever gets padding. A full-bleed hero must be an outer wrapper with an inner .wrap, not a .wrap override.

Reduced motion: the blanket rule (global.css line 83) uses only *, which does not match ::before or ::after. Blobs or sheens drawn as pseudo-elements would keep animating, so use *, *::before, *::after. It also does not stop Web Animations API calls, rAF loops, Three.js uniforms or ::view-transition-* pseudo-elements, which each need an explicit matchMedia check or a CSS override. Galaxy.astro reads reduce once at init with no change listener; the new intro ignite, blob morph and parallax must all check it and render a static frame.

Scroll and gesture hijack if the galaxy becomes a full-bleed hero: .galaxy has touch-action: none, and OrbitControls enables wheel zoom with preventDefault. A full-width hero would trap page scrolling on phones and swallow wheel scrolling on desktop. Set touch-action: pan-y, set controls.enableZoom = false (keep the + and − buttons), or require an explicit 'Explore' activation. Keep the controls reachable by keyboard.

backdrop-filter cost: a sticky glass header (and glass footer) over a WebGL canvas that redraws every frame forces a re-blur every frame. That is costly on low-end Android and iOS, and .g-controls already blurs five buttons over the canvas. Mitigations: blur 12px or less; apply frost only after scrolling past the hero; never put backdrop-filter on repeated items (.case, .rows li, 100+ posts, filter chips); no glass-over-glass; include -webkit-backdrop-filter; provide an @supports fallback. backdrop-filter also creates a containing block, so a position: fixed mobile menu inside the header would be positioned relative to the header.

Blob rendering cost: animating border-radius or SVG path morphs together with filter: blur(30px) on large elements repaints every frame. Animate only transform and opacity on pre-blurred assets, or do the blobs in the existing WebGL context; do not add a second context. mix-blend-mode on large layers is also expensive.

WebGL load: a full-bleed canvas at setPixelRatio(min(dpr, 2)) on a 2560px monitor is about 5120x2880 pixels. Cap the DPR around 1.5 or cap the total pixel count. three.module is 753KB minified (about 190KB gzipped), so keep the IntersectionObserver lazy start, but because it will be above the fold, show a CSS glow or blob poster first for LCP. Render on demand (or at reduced fps) when auto-rotate is off and nothing changes, instead of 60fps forever. pick() projects all 300 nodes on every pointermove, which is fine today but should be throttled if blobs and wireframes add more objects.

Transparent-canvas halos: Galaxy.astro deliberately keeps an opaque scene background because starMat writes alpha 1.0 with additive blending. Switching to alpha: true so CSS glow and blobs show through requires the fragment shader to output premultiplied alpha (alpha = max colour channel); otherwise each sprite paints a dark square over the page.

Long-form reading on dark: pure #fff on near-black causes halation. Use #ece8fb to #e9e6f5 text, keep line-height 1.72, keep Source Serif 4 at weight 400 (light display cuts look thinner on dark), and keep the measure at about 42rem. Do not place animated glow, blobs or galaxy behind .prose. A stationary background with constant contrast is required, and there should be no motion near reading content. Body links in full-saturation neon over long paragraphs vibrate, so use a softened tint with underlines. --ink-soft must stay at 4.5:1 or above on every surface, including over the hero glow (#b9b1d8 on #2b1466 is 7.4:1, fine) and on glass bars (about 6.1:1).

Vietnamese diacritics with an artistic display face: Buljirya itself cannot be used (personal-use licence and only about 222 glyphs, no ặ ẫ ở ữ ự). Choose only families with Google's vietnamese subset (verified: Fraunces, Playfair, Yeseva One, Prata, Cormorant, Literata, Noto Serif Display, Unbounded; Bodoni Moda, DM Serif Display, Instrument Serif, Gloock, Young Serif, Abril Fatface, Italiana and Syne lack it). The current hero h1 line-height of 1.02 and -0.035em tracking will collide or clip stacked marks on capitals. Line-mask text reveals (overflow: hidden per line) clip tone marks above the cap height. background-clip: text gradient headlines with tight line-height make marks outside the box invisible. So add padding-block, keep line-height at 1.1 or more, and test 'Ẫ Ở Ữ Ự ặ' at every display size. Wide-tracked all-caps Vietnamese subtitles are legible but are a templated tell according to the frontend-design skill, so keep them to one lockup.

Font payload: Fraunces with four axes plus Vietnamese, Latin and Latin-ext subsets adds roughly 100–200KB per subset. Restrict the axis ranges in the css2 URL, preload only the display weight used above the fold, and keep display=swap. Stacked-diacritic fallback metrics shift layout on swap; size-adjust or ascent-override on a local fallback can reduce the CLS.

Theme logic: making dark the default via the :root tokens breaks three things that key off [data-theme=dark] or prefers-color-scheme. Shiki .astro-code would render github-light white blocks; the mermaid 'neutral' theme would be dark-on-dark; and color-scheme stays light, so the native search input, clear button and scrollbars render light. Users with a stored localStorage theme=light would land on a light page that still clashes. Either drop light mode or make it a deliberate reading mode with darkened accents (neon on white fails: cyan 1.38:1, amber 1.75:1, magenta 3.19:1).

Brutalist on dark: --edge and the hard shadows reference var(--ink), which becomes near-white, giving glaring white slabs. Hard-coded #fff on eosin (.brutal .status, .cta .button:hover) fails at 2.44:1 in the dark set. The 8px right margins (.brutal .case, .article-head.brutal) exist to fit the shadow and must stay if the shadow offset changes.

Images: public/vault-assets is 62MB (306 files, PNG screenshots up to 1.2MB, uncompressed JPG field photos). The tags have no loading=lazy, decoding or width/height, so CLS and data cost are real on mobile, and adding more imagery multiplies that. Generate resized WebP/AVIF with sharp (already in node_modules) and add intrinsic dimensions. The 65 SVG diagrams and white screenshots must not be colour-inverted for dark mode (colour-coded biology); frame them instead. Exclude dissection photos (dvcxs-*) from decorative use.

Overflow and sticky: blobs that bleed off the viewport rely on body { overflow-x: hidden }. If someone also sets overflow on html, body becomes the scroll container and the sticky glass header breaks. Prefer overflow-x: clip on the hero wrapper.

Hero text over the galaxy: bright core sprites, labels (.g-label with neon text-shadow) and blobs passing under the headline make contrast vary frame to frame. Keep the composition asymmetric (camera setViewOffset or target shift so the galaxy centre sits at about 65–70% x), and add a static radial scrim behind the text column. Labels must not overlap the h1 at 390px.

Galaxy.astro hard-coded colours (the neon map, #ffd6f5 and #7a5cff core, #cfd8ff background stars, #ffffff highlight lines) and the CSS rgba values in .g-* will drift from the new tokens unless they are centralised. graph.json topic ids (biology, french, business, ai-development, university-courses, english) are the key for any per-topic colour reuse in chips and covers.

Motion restraint (frontend-design skill): the brief pins a dark fluid direction, but scattered fade-ups, hover lifts on every row and filter chip, or animated blur on core flows would read as templated and hurt the 'clear and minimal' requirement for blog, search, tables and 404. Keep motion to the hero, the CTA and the portfolio pages.

judgements.winner: Màng mỏng (Thin Film): the whole site moves into the galaxy's violet space

scores.name: Màng mỏng (Thin Film): the whole site moves into the galaxy's violet space
scores.notes: This is the closest match to the reference the owner sent. It has the deep violet void with a radial glow, glossy iridescent blobs bleeding off the right edge (normal blending with fresnel, so they read as filled liquid like the reference rather than hollow rims), white wireframe polyhedra with vertex dots, frosted header and footer bars, solid white icon squares in the footer, and small glass buttons. It is the only direction that keeps the FLUID/TECHNOLOGY lockup: big light display type plus one wide-tracked subtitle. It also gives the most motion (ignition, morphing blobs, rotating topic polyhedra, parallax, sheen, CTA spin, brutal press, PhaseTrack fill), which is literally what 'thêm các loại hiệu ứng motion' asks for, and it still keeps the core flows still. Noto Serif Display gets the most Buljirya-like flourish here: weight 300 in the hero, italic wordmark and CTA, and condensed weight 650 on project pages. Cohesion is the strongest of the three. The galaxy background equals --void, the canvas runs under the header, the topic stars become the polyhedra, and a static vesicle layer in the gutter carries the motif onto every page. Weaknesses: (1) It is dark-only and deletes the theme toggle, so readers of long Vietnamese notes lose a light option. (2) It retunes the arm hues of the galaxy the owner said they like. (3) Links in --link #8fdcff are close to biology cyan, which blurs the 'neon means topic' logic. (4) It renames the hero to 'Bộ não thứ hai' without the owner's approval. (5) Covers and OG PNGs go into public/, which bloats the git and R2 sync. (6) It is the heaviest WebGL budget: 5 detail-5 icospheres plus hulls, a scroll dolly and parallax. Grafts from the other two fix most of these.

scores.name: Dark-field Bloom (Trường tối phát quang)
scores.notes: This is the most original biology concept: dark-field microscopy, ctenophore comb-row iridescence and Haeckel radiolarians. 'Plankton flash on disturbance' is a delightful pointer-triggered effect that costs one uniform write per event. It keeps the original neon arm colours as fluorescence channels, so the galaxy doesn't drift. The sharp-generated LUT photo variants are cheaper and more honest than a CSS duotone. The opt-in 'Trường sáng' bright-field mode, with darkened stain variants, preserves the old H&E work and gives readers a light option, and the new storage key 'field' avoids stale theme=light. It moves further from the reference the owner pointed at, though. The additive, rim-only cells read as hollow bubbles, not the reference's glossy opaque liquid. The galaxy sits inside a circular eyepiece mask rather than bleeding off the edge. The tracked subtitle is dropped, and the primary button is an iris gradient (closer to a template tell than the reference's glass buttons). Italic display is used only for Latin species names. That is a lovely scholarly detail, but it gives the owner less of the 'artistic font' feel they asked for. The two-theme upkeep (Shiki, mermaid, stain variants) adds cost.

scores.name: Huỳnh quang: neon brutalism for a dark-field microscope
scores.notes: This is the most disciplined and most implementable plan. Making the canvas transparent (alpha true, star alpha = max(rgb)) lets the CSS glow show through with no seam risk, which is technically the cleanest galaxy integration. Covers and OG images are prerendered Astro endpoints, so nothing bloats public/ or the vault-to-R2 sync. The excitation plays once per session. Each project gets one channel colour (--c), and links use periwinkle, outside the channel set, so neon keeps its topic meaning. A data-field='dark' lock keeps the hero dark even in the opt-in bright-field mode. It also covers forced-colors, the drawing-buffer cap and an LCP-safe opacity .01 start. But pass 2 deliberately cut the PhaseTrack fill, the CTA sheen and spin, and the scroll dolly, leaving a single unprompted moment, while the owner explicitly asked to ADD motion effects. Like B, it drops the tracked subtitle that makes the reference's FLUID/TECHNOLOGY lockup. The fluorescence concept largely overlaps B and is slightly less vivid. The hollow ghost-frame brutal shadow is clever but fragile: it shows as a dark rectangle on anything other than --void. The 999px pill chips also break the reference's rectangular button language.

judgements.winner: Màng mỏng (Thin Film): the whole site moves into the galaxy's violet space

scores.name: Màng mỏng (Thin Film): the whole site moves into the galaxy's violet space
scores.notes: Of the three, this one does the most of what the user asked for. It covers all four parts: (1) the whole site moves into the galaxy's own --void, with scene.background set to the same hex, so the seam is gone; (2) the motion follows the reference's grammar (iridescent blobs, wireframes with vertex dots, glass bars, white icon squares in the footer); (3) a Didone as the Buljirya stand-in; (4) a full image plan. It is the only direction that builds the topic polyhedra into the galaxy itself, and it uses one shared topics.ts for the galaxy, chips, covers and CSS, so the colours can't drift apart. Accessibility is the most thorough of the three: contrast ratios are computed for every token, --edge passes 3:1, the white-on-eosin pill is fixed, the reduced-motion rule covers ::before/::after with a live matchMedia listener, the rotate button is relabelled as a WCAG 2.2.2 pause control, the canvas uses touch-action pan-y and enableZoom=false, buttons are 44px, and the 404 avoids the padding shorthand. Core flows stay flat and still on --deep, and the empty state comes with a reset action. Weaknesses: (a) dark-only means no light option for long notes. Reading on dark is well tuned (#e4dff5, 40rem, 18/1.75), but light reading is only promised for 'later'. (b) The blob spec is technically wrong: IcosahedronGeometry(r,5) is about 720 triangles, not 50k, and dFdx/dFdy normals give flat facets, so the blobs would look low-poly instead of liquid. (c) The h1 starts at opacity 0, which delays LCP. (d) There is too much motion: the scroll-linked camera dolly, the conic CTA spin and the sheen all sit on top of the ignition. (e) It retunes all six arm colours of a galaxy the user said they like. (f) OG PNGs go into public/og/, and npm run publish does git add -A, so every sync commit grows. (g) The tracked all-caps subtitle copies the reference literally and is a known templated tell. (h) The hero copy change needs the owner's approval. The scope is large, but having one theme keeps it maintainable. It keeps the opaque scene background, which is correct: the current Galaxy.astro comment records that a transparent canvas gives dark halos.

scores.name: Dark-field Bloom (Trường tối phát quang)
scores.notes: This is the most original and the most personal concept: dark-field microscopy, comb-jelly iridescence, Haeckel radiolarians, fluorescence LUT photos, and display italic kept for Latin species names. It suits a biology learner without becoming kitsch. It keeps the six galaxy hexes exactly, builds the iris DataTexture from the same stops as the CSS, and reads the scene's outer stop from --abyss, so cohesion is excellent. Its strongest motion is the plankton flash on pointer or tap: it responds to the user, costs one uniform write and carries the biological story. Readability is the best of the three because a bright-field reading mode is offered as an opt-in under a new storage key, and it reuses the H&E palette with stain variants that are all at least 4.99:1. The table scroller is focusable and the 404 page includes search. It loses fidelity because the user asked for something 'hơi giống kiểu trên ảnh' (somewhat like the image). Additive, rim-only dark-field cells are translucent halos, not the reference's glossy, saturated liquid blobs. The circular eyepiece mask also turns the free right-side bleed into a contained porthole, which comes close to the 'galaxy in a box' look that caused the complaint. Other gaps: there is no explicit pause control for the drifting cells (WCAG 2.2.2). The search input's 8px radius breaks its own 3px rule for controls. The cyan plus magenta double misregistration shadow is loud right under the galaxy. Keeping two themes in sync (Shiki, Mermaid re-render, stain variants) adds ongoing work.

scores.name: Huỳnh quang: neon brutalism for a dark-field microscope
scores.notes: This is the most disciplined direction and has the best engineering hygiene. Covers and OG images are prerendered endpoints, so nothing lands in public/ or in the publish commits. It caps the drawing buffer at about 3MP and drops blobs on low-end devices. The excitation reveal runs once per session, the h1 starts at opacity .01 so LCP is unaffected, and it handles forced-colors. The periwinkle link sits outside the channel hues, so neon keeps its topic meaning, and the brightfield mode keeps the hero dark. Readability is very good: no glow anywhere near the prose, #ddd8f2 body text, and opt-in light reading. Weaknesses: the user explicitly asked to add more kinds of motion ('thêm các loại hiệu ứng motion'), and this direction cuts the PhaseTrack fill, the sheen, the CTA border and the dolly, so it under-delivers on a stated request. Switching the galaxy to a transparent alpha canvas goes against the existing Galaxy.astro comment, which says additive sprites show dark halos, so the star shader would need reworking. Each project frame gets a channel colour (Cyclistic in cyan), which clashes with the rule that cyan means biology and weakens its own 'colour is a legend' idea. The hollow ghost frame only works when --void sits behind it. The 999px pill chips don't match the reference's rectangular buttons. The concept overlaps Dark-field Bloom but is less rich.

judgements.winner: Màng mỏng (Thin Film): the whole site moves into the galaxy's violet space

scores.name: Màng mỏng (Thin Film): the whole site moves into the galaxy's violet space
scores.notes:
Closest to the reference: the blob column bleeds off the right edge, the header and footer are glass bars, white wireframes carry vertex dots, the footer has white icon squares, the buttons are small glass rectangles, and there is one tracked subtitle. The brief pins that look, so the one tracked line is acceptable. It also answers 'thêm các loại hiệu ứng motion' most fully.

Engineering strengths:
- Dark-only is the biggest maintainability win of the three. It deletes the theme toggle, the two prefers-color-scheme/[data-theme] blocks, the Shiki dual-theme `!important` overrides in global.css (lines 55-59) and the bootstrap logic in Base.astro.
- It keeps the OPAQUE scene background. Galaxy.astro explicitly warns that a transparent canvas gives the additive sprites and lines dark halos, so this is the safe choice. The only change is that the CanvasTexture gradient becomes --void plus a CSS mask.
- One WebGL context.
- Header frost is applied only after the hero leaves view.
- A single src/data/topics.ts feeds Galaxy, Cover and the CSS, so the colours can't drift.
- The specificity and gutter guards are correct.

Weaknesses:
(1) Scope is the largest of the three: 13 motion items, including scroll dolly, parallax, ignition, polyhedra hover, hulls, sheen, conic CTA, PhaseTrack fill, view transitions and the duotone filter.
(2) In three r187, IcosahedronGeometry(r,5) is about 720 triangles, not 50k. With dFdx/dFdy normals and noise displacement the blobs will look visibly faceted. Use detail about 16-20, or analytic normals.
(3) The h1 tween starts at opacity 0, which can delay LCP.
(4) The OG PNGs go into public/, and `npm run publish` does `git add -A`, so they bloat every sync commit.
(5) --link #8fdcff and --focus #4cd8ff are nearly the biology hue, which blurs the topic-colour semantics.
(6) Retuning the arm hexes slightly changes the galaxy the user said they liked.
(7) The runtime SVG feColorMatrix duotone and the mask-image on the canvas add compositing cost. Both are acceptable.

scores.name: Dark-field Bloom (Trường tối phát quang)
scores.notes:
The most subject-grounded concept: dark-field optics, plankton that flash when disturbed, fluorescence LUTs and channel misregistration. It departs further from the reference, though:
- The circular eyepiece mask reintroduces a 'window' around the galaxy, partly the boxed feeling the user complained about.
- The additive, rim-lit cells read as ghostly, not the glossy liquid blobs in the image.
- It drops the reference's tracked subtitle.

Engineering pluses:
- Additive cells match the existing additive pipeline, so there are no blending surprises.
- The plankton flash costs one uniform write per event and is the best cheap 'motion that answers the user'.
- The iris DataTexture built from the same stops as the CSS keeps WebGL and CSS in sync.
- Build-time sharp LUT photos (greyscale().linear()) need no runtime filter or blend at all.
- The static CSS poster under the canvas covers LCP without a screenshot step.
- Brutal frames use a pure double box-shadow (cyan 4px plus magenta 8px), with no pseudo-element or stacking-context dependency.
- The neon hexes are unchanged.

Minuses:
- Keeping bright-field means two token sets, six stained variants, a Shiki swap and a mermaid re-init, all permanent upkeep.
- The circular mask needs extra code to fade labels outside the circle and to keep it off the controls.
- The uChannel[6] array plus a per-star arm attribute is a moderate refactor.
- IcosahedronGeometry(r,4) is about 500 triangles, so the fresnel rims will show facets.
- OG PNGs again go into public/.
- Radii are inconsistent: search 8px, chips 3px.

scores.name: Huỳnh quang: neon brutalism for a dark-field microscope
scores.notes:
It has the most restraint and the best performance hygiene. It caps the drawing buffer at about 3 MP rather than only capping DPR, runs the excitation once per session via sessionStorage, starts the h1 at opacity .01 for LCP, throttles pick() to rAF, and adds a forced-colors fallback.

It also has the best build architecture: covers and OG images come from prerendered Astro endpoints (covers/[slug].svg.ts, og/[slug].png.ts), so nothing is committed to public/. That matters because `npm run publish` runs `git add -A`.

The link colour (periwinkle) sits outside the channel set, so neon keeps its topic meaning. That is better than the other two.

Weaknesses:
- It explicitly cuts the sheen, CTA spin, PhaseTrack fill and scroll dolly, while the user asked to ADD varied motion. That costs fidelity.
- The transparent-canvas rewrite (alpha:true, alpha=max(rgb)) contradicts the documented reason Galaxy.astro uses an opaque background. LineBasicMaterial cannot output that alpha without onBeforeCompile or a custom ShaderMaterial, so it is the riskiest single item across all three directions.
- The ghost-frame box-shadow (spread -3px filled with --void) breaks on any non-void background, as the direction itself admits.
- Colouring projects by topic channel (Cyclistic in biology cyan) muddles the legend.
- Like B, it carries dual-theme upkeep.
- The concept overlaps Dark-field Bloom but is less developed.
- Pill chips at 999px drift from the reference's rectangles.
